decision: Do not patch CPU reciprocal or hardcode a q correction. Add explicit stage-scoped observed-operand consistency evidence; keep the original FP32 math gate and frozen source-path results.

existing_reference.limitation: CPU correctly-rounded 127/amax and 1/inverse do not model the two approximate reciprocal instructions in this original binary. Keep the result as source-math evidence.

next_revision_additions.component: observed D4 operand CPU dot reference
next_revision_additions.behavior: For arbitrary supported M,N,K (K padded to 128), decode block (k//128)*M+m, float d4[(k%128)//32] and signed qs[k%128]. Read original Q8_0 half weight scale and 32 signed codes. Compute float32(weight_scale*d4)*float32(int_dot), then double accumulation. Accept operand bytes/hash/provenance as explicit input; never recalculate q via CPU division and never override values by row or k index.

Add separately named fields for source_math_path, main_operand_consistency, conversion_contract_status, and original_fp32_math_pass. With the present conversion-only replay use consistency evidence, not main pass or complete conversion pass.

A later root-run original main/fixup replay must consume the same owned D4 bytes that the CPU reference uses, with original captured function identity and dimensions preserved. Only then can main_given_operand_pass validate that stage. No original conversion pool read is needed.

Validate actual q/d4 against an independently justified reciprocal/rounding/FTZ contract. Normal-domain interval candidates may be used only after the numerical contract is bound to the deployed binary. Zero blocks, subnormals, extreme magnitudes, infinities and NaNs require explicit defined handling; unsupported is not passed.

unchanged_requirements: Existing numerical tolerance and old rejection records.
No LLM actual outputs or performance-fitting data.
No binary changes, GPU execution or runtime benchmarks in this audit.
present_acceptance_state: Existing source-path gate remains failed for 60 of the 64 row11 samples. The new evidence does not change that status.
why_observed_operands_do_not_validate_co: A wrong quantizer can produce wrong operands and a perfectly correct main kernel can consume them. The main_given_operand reference would agree, so independent conversion validation and original end-to-end math validation remain necessary.
why_current_replay_is_only_consistency: The current owned conversion replay output was not directly observed as the operand of the original graph main launch. Same function/input and 64 exact archived graph matches are strong consistency evidence, not a proof of the actual pool bytes or every main output.
